src/blocks/blockGuards.ts:10-18. The doc comment at line 10 says what the claim states. The code returns undefined unless Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(blockRenderers, type) is true (line 15), and then returns the value only if typeof is 'function' (line 17). Traces: (1) A blockRenderers with no own toString: customRendererFor(br,'toString') fails the own check and returns undefined, so inherited Object.prototype names such as toString, constructor and valueOf are never returned. (2) Object.create(null): hasOwnProperty is borrowed via .call, so there is no TypeError and own keys still work. (3) An own hasOwnProperty override on blockRenderers is not consulted, because Object.prototype's version is invoked via .call. (4) A non-function own value returns undefined. Absolute-claim input: a host that registers its own toString function property returns that function. This matches the doc's 'own function property only', since the doc's 'never an Object.prototype name' reads as never an inherited one. A deliberately registered own property is the intended case. Absent blockRenderers returns undefined (line 15).

node_modules/react-chatbot-kit/package.json (v2.2.2) has main build/index.js, no `type`, no `module`, no `exports`, so Node treats it as CommonJS. build/index.js is a webpack bundle that builds namespace object t via e.d(t,{Chatbot:()=>B,...,default:()=>H}) (getter defineProperty) and ends with `module.exports=t`. There is no literal `exports.Chatbot =`, so Node's cjs-module-lexer cannot detect named exports and `import { Chatbot }` under Node ESM fails. A default import yields the whole module.exports object, which is why ChatWidget.tsx:58 unwraps `.Chatbot ?? chatbotKit`. The comment at ChatWidget.tsx:53-57 matches. I did not run Node itself.

node_modules/react-chatbot-kit (v2.2.2, main build/index.js) is a webpack CJS bundle ending in `module.exports=t`, where t is defined via e.d(t,{Chatbot:()=>B,...,default:()=>H,...}) with H=B and __esModule set (e.r(t)). So under __esModule interop (bundlers/TS esModuleInterop) the default import is t.default = B, the component itself; B is a plain function component with no Chatbot property, so `.Chatbot ?? chatbotKit` yields B. Under Node ESM (no __esModule honoring) the default import is module.exports = t, whose Chatbot property is B, so the unwrap yields B. Types: build/src/index.d.ts has `export default Chatbot` and named Chatbot, matching the cast in src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:58 (import at line 26). Absolute-claim trace: an object lacking both would be the break; the bundle exports both forms as the same B. Evidence read from the minified bundle via targeted matches, not the full file.

ChatWidget.tsx:231-237 keepInsideViewport useCallback has deps [dimensions] (whole object), so its identity changes whenever dimensions state gets a new object. ChatWidget.tsx:232 setDimensions updater returns prev when prev.maxWidth === window.innerWidth, else a new object with maxWidth updated (only dimensions recreated once). Line 234-235 setPosition returns prev when clampPosition x,y are unchanged. clampPosition (119-125) is idempotent: x=max(0,min(x,vw-w)); reapplying yields the same value, including when vw-w<0 (gives 0 both times). Open effect (257-259) depends on [isOpen, keepInsideViewport]; keepInsideViewport changes only with dimensions (237). First run may change maxWidth, causing one rerun; the second run returns prev for both states, so no state change and no further rerun. Position-only changes do not recreate the callback. Absolute-input check: width shrink while open and viewport narrower than window width, traced above; settles.

ChatWidget.tsx:603-625: position fixed (610); percentages on a fixed element resolve against the viewport unless an ancestor has transform/filter (then that ancestor's box), as the comment says. CSS min-width overrides max-width, as stated. Trace 390px viewport: minWidth=min(300,max(390,195))=300, maxWidth=390, so a remembered width of e.g. 800px is clamped to 390; a small window is floored at 300 (capped at 100% when 100% >= 50vw). Transformed 100px ancestor: minWidth=min(300,max(100,195))=195 (50vw floor, assuming 390px viewport), which beats maxWidth 100px, so the window stays 195px wide and visible. minHeight uses the same pattern with 50dvh; maxHeight=min(maxHeight,100%). Explicit width/height (606-607) are subject to these limits. The comment matches the implementation.

ChatWidget.tsx:621-624 sets minWidth=min(Npx, max(100%, 50vw)), minHeight=min(Npx, max(100%, 50dvh)), maxHeight=min(Npx, 100%), maxWidth='100%' as separate inline style properties. Per CSS and React inline styles (applied via the CSSOM), a value with an unsupported function or unit is rejected and only that declaration is dropped, leaving the property unset, while the separate maxWidth '100%' declaration is unaffected. package.json and README.md declare no browserslist or supported-browsers statement (searched for browserslist, browser, dvh, Safari, Chrome; only tsconfig target ES2020 appears), so the project makes no support commitment that the expressions would break. The claim describes the code and CSS fallback behavior accurately.

ChatController.activity (ChatController.ts:189) is incremented only at handleUserInput (:244) and runCommandInput (:257). Typed text goes through handleUserInput; slash commands (typed, or via open({command}) at ChatWidget.tsx:457) go through runCommandInput; so every user turn and command bumps it. addMessages (:206-209), reply, sendTurn, performTurn, newConversation and switchConversation never touch it. newConversation instead triggers host.onNewConversation -> remountChat (ChatWidget.tsx:330-334, 307-310), which increments requestedResetKeyRef; History switch (loadConversation non-restore) also calls remountChat (:402). ChatWidget.tsx:389-394 abandons the restore on activity or reset-key change, and :424-431 keeps a failed saved ID likewise. This matches the claim; appendBlocks (addMessages) leaves activity unchanged.

ChatWidget.tsx:384-394 snapshots controller.activity and requestedResetKeyRef and skips the restore if either changed. Turns (ChatController.handleUserInput:244), commands (runCommandInput:257), new conversation (onNewConversation -> remountChat, ChatWidget.tsx:330-333) and a successful History switch (remountChat at :402) all change one of them, so the comment holds for those. Counterexample: a History switch whose getConversation rejects while the restore is pending. loadConversation returns false at :404-406 without remountChat, and switchToConversation (:441-444) calls controller.reply, which only calls addMessages (ChatController.ts:313-315) and does not bump activity or the reset key. The restore then resolves, passes the guard, calls switchConversation(saved) and remountChat. That replaces the error reply and moves the user to the saved conversation. A failed switch arguably was never 'made', so the comment may be literally accurate. I found no unchanged requirement file (no .src instruction files in the head view) showing that a failed switch must win, so I cannot grade FAIL or INVALID.

ChatController.ts:78-82 declares onTurnFailed?: (text: string) => boolean | void, with TSDoc saying the text is what the user typed and true means it went back into the composer. The call site at ChatController.ts:419 passes `text` and sets refilled = (result === true). Lines 421-423 restage the attachments only if refilled, attachments exist and nothing new is staged. ChatWidget.tsx:349-355 returns false when the input is missing (!input) or has a non-empty value. Otherwise it calls setChatInputValue(input, failedText) and returns true. Two details are slightly looser than the claim wording. ChatWidget.tsx:349-355: onTurnFailed queries the kit input, returns false if absent or if `input.value` is truthy, and only then calls setChatInputValue (SlashAutocomplete.tsx:29-33, which sets the native value and dispatches an input event). Whitespace-only text is a truthy string, so it is treated as typing and not overwritten (refill skipped), which matches the comment. The check reads the live DOM value, which is the most current typed text. A native input event updates the kit's controlled state synchronously, so text typed but not yet committed to kit state cannot hide behind an empty DOM value. If the DOM still holds not-yet-cleared sent text, the check fails safe by skipping the refill. The check and the write are synchronous with no gap for typing to intervene. Absolute-claim input traced: whitespace-only composer, and kit state differing from DOM. Neither overwrites existing text.

The comment at ChatWidget.tsx:506 says a handle kept past unmount 'does nothing'. Only appendBlocks (517-520) checks aliveRef. The other handle methods (useImperativeHandle 566-578) have no such guard. setLayout is changeLayout (190-195), which calls storage.set('layout', mode) after unmount. open() and close() go through setOpen (170-183), which calls storage.set('open', ...) when initialOpen==='remember'. newConversation calls controller.newConversation() on the disposed widget's controller. So a kept handle still does persistent work (storage writes) after unmount, and the absolute wording is wrong. I did not read the storage implementation. The counterexample is the unguarded setLayout, which reaches storage.set. This is a comment inaccuracy only, and the behavior is mostly harmless.

types.ts:303-310 declares appendBlocks(blocks: Block[]): void with TSDoc: buffered before first open, kept over saved-conversation restore, dropped by new conversation or History switch, lost on reload. ChatWidget.tsx:515-553 matches. After the aliveRef check (517-520) it warns and returns after unmount. Non-array input gets console.error and returns (521-524). Malformed blocks are filtered with a warn (525-527). Blank blocks are dropped with a warn when answerToMessages yields nothing (540-544). Unknown custom types only warn, and renderers are looked up at render time through blockRenderers (530-539). Appended messages are recorded in appendedRef (545). If the Chatbot for the latest reset is mounted they go live via controller.addMessages with no remount, otherwise they seed initialMessages (549-550), which covers buffering before the first open. onNewConversation (330-331) and the loadConversation non-restore path (379, 396) clear appendedRef, so a new conversation or History switch drops them. A restore re-includes appendedRef (396-401), so appended blocks are kept. useImperativeHandle exposes appendBlocks (575), and mount.tsx:74 forwards it. Implementation matches the declaration and docs.

Every README.md statement on appendBlocks matches ChatWidget.tsx. README:73 lists appendBlocks(blocks) on the handle, and ChatWidget.tsx:575 exposes it. README:75 says it adds an assistant message with no user turn: answerToMessages -> controller.addMessages at ChatWidget.tsx:540-549. It says blocks appended before the first open appear when it opens: mountedResetKeyRef is null before hasOpened (:499-501), so the messages go to initialMessages (:550), which seeds the mount. It says they stay over the saved-conversation restore: loadConversation with restore keeps appendedRef and re-adds it (:396-401). It says a new conversation drops them (onNewConversation clears appendedRef, :330-336) and a History switch drops them (non-restore load sets appendedRef=[], :396). It says they live only in the widget: appendedRef and initialMessages hold them and nothing goes to the data source or storage. README:131 and :204 cover custom types through blockRenderers, and :120 mentions appendBlocks. Unknown types without a renderer only warn at :530-539; the README says such blocks are skipped, which fits renderers being looked up at render time. The README does not describe live append while open or closed, or how invalid input is reported (console.error/warn and ignore, :517-544). Those are omissions, not contradictions, and the code does what the README implies (append is live when the chat is mounted, :549).
